evidence: The diff hunk shows `live_shared` calling `folded` with no negativity check, and `record_shared` writing `str(ceiling)`, which `parse_ceiling` reads back as a signed delta. The agent reproduced it (`ceiling=200000` on both stops) and moved the `ceiling < 0` check into `folded`, the one function both folds pass through.
guidance_note: When splitting one validated computation into two callers, move the validation into the shared function in the original PR, and test the new path with an input the old check used to reject.

evidence: `shared_at_start` runs on every Stop and writes one record per session with no pruning, so growth is unbounded as the reviewer says. The reviewer's minimum ask was a note. The agent documented the cost in the README and deferred pruning to a ticket, explaining that deleting a live session's record silently re-freezes it, which is the bug this PR fixes.
guidance_note: When a design adds a per-entity persistent file, state its retention cost in the docs in the same PR rather than leaving it to a reviewer to discover.

evidence: Same defect as F1: a negative shared fold is serialized as `-50000` and re-read as an adjustment, giving 200,000. It was fixed once, in 9bea2ce, by moving the check into `folded`, and the agent reports two mutation-checked tests.
guidance_note: When a value is round-tripped through a grammar that also expresses deltas, test the round trip at the sign boundary before shipping.

evidence: A partial is left behind if the process is killed between `write_text` and `os.replace`, but `record_shared` is reached only while the session has no record, so each session directory sees essentially one write attempt. 'Accumulate indefinitely' therefore overstates it. Folding the cleanup into the retention ticket rather than adding a glob-delete on every write is sound.

The README sentence attaches 'gets the new number' to all three cases, but `ceiling_in` calls `sys.exit` on a malformed line, and the PR's own test asserts that a new session fails loudly. The agent split the sentence case by case.
guidance_note: Before shipping docs written from a fact sheet, check each consequence clause against the test that pins it, especially when one sentence lists several causes.

evidence: In the CHANGELOG, 'A session that starts after the edit still reads it and gets the new number' directly follows the syntax-error sentence. That makes the false claim a second time, and the agent edited it independently of the README.
guidance_note: When the same behaviour is described in README and CHANGELOG, verify both copies against the code in the same pass.

evidence: `shared_at_start` keys on `session_id` and short-circuits forever, and the agent confirmed that `finalize-session` resets in-process, so the id survives. The agent conceded this is a regression the PR introduces. The reviewer explicitly offered 'accepting and documenting this as a known limitation'. Documenting it and filing ticket i2m is defensible, because the obvious fix runs through the fragile `closed_out`.
guidance_note: When keying state on an identifier, list every lifecycle event that preserves that identifier (here, an in-place reset) during design, and decide about each one in the PR rather than talking past it.

narrative: Seven first-round findings on the shared-ceiling freeze, with clean approval in round 1. The one real bug (F1/F3, a negative shared fold reinterpreted as a delta) was fixed once at the root, by moving the check into the shared `folded` function. Doc mismatches were fixed in both copies. Retention, stray partials, and reset-in-place staleness were documented and deferred to linked tickets. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The agent reproduced every bug claim against real files before planning, and corrected the reviewer's analysis where it understated the defect (the bug fails on the first stop too).
Two duplicate findings (F1/F3, F5/F6) were handled with one fix each but replied to separately, which kept every thread's resolution traceable.

evidence: The usage line said '2 bad argv, or no transport', but `mkdir`, self-path resolution, and the claude-process lookups also exit 2. The agent broadened it to '2 anything that stopped it — argv, setup, or transport' in 9a30742. Its verification counted only explicit `exit 2`s and missed the implicit `set -e` exits, which is what F6 later found.
guidance_note: Before asserting an exhaustive exit-code contract in a `set -e` script, enumerate implicit failures (unguarded command substitutions and redirections), not just explicit `exit` statements.

evidence: The reviewer's 'silently keep asserting' is wrong, because both constants are asserted against real exit status. But the agent's own F1 fix in the same commit, 9a30742, declared 2 the launcher's single failure code, which contradicts the 'two distinct facts' pushback it committed alongside. The agent reversed it in 9540a64, collapsing to one `REFUSED_RC`.
guidance_note: When pushing back on a same-fact duplication, check whether a fix being pushed in the same commit already states the contract that makes them one fact.

evidence: The parser checks only `${1:-}` against `--*`, so any single-line message whose first word starts with `--` is refused, not just a bare two-dash token. 9a30742 rewrote the README to 'Put `--` first when the message begins with a two-dash word, whatever comes after it'. The reply-hint says already_fixed, but the agent actually fixed it in response.
guidance_note: Describe a parser's refusal by the exact predicate it evaluates (first token matches `--*`), not by an illustrative example.

evidence: `finalize-session --help` in the Modes block reads as an invocation shape and is not one. Restoring the full argv would recreate the second copy that had already gone stale (`[message...]` without `--goal`/`--reset`). Pointing at `_usage` is the reviewer's second option, done well.

9a30742 (F1's fix) rewrote the exit line's 2-half and left '0 recorded', which `--help` (`_usage; exit 0`, recording nothing) falsifies. The agent itself called it 'the second round in which this line has been wrong by naming a subset'. It replaced the line with a non-enumerating '0 it did what you asked'.
guidance_note: When a finding shows one clause of a contract line enumerates a subset, check every clause of that line against every path before pushing the fix.

evidence: The exhaustive '2 — argv, setup, or transport' claim came from F1's fix (9a30742). The four `mktemp` assignments were unguarded under `set -euo pipefail` and exited 1, which the agent confirmed against the pre-guard script. The agent fixed the code, not the sentence, with `_mktemp_or_exit` in 9540a64.
guidance_note: When a fix writes down an exhaustive failure contract, grep the arm for every command that can fail under errexit and guard or test each before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 9540a64 touched only the launcher's mktemp sites and tests, and both the README usage line and the `_usage` 'written down once' comment date from the original PR. The only divergence is shell quotes around a placeholder in a bash fence, which is not drift. The real kernel was the overclaiming `_usage` comment, and that is what was cut.
guidance_note: Don't write a uniqueness claim ('written down once') in a comment unless a grep confirms no other copy exists in the repo.

evidence: 9540a64's helper prints `cannot create the $purpose tempfile in ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`, while the test-fixture comment in the same commit says macOS `mktemp -t` ignores `$TMPDIR`. The fix's own operator-facing text contradicted what the fix had just learned. The directory was dropped from both the message and the helper comment.
guidance_note: When the investigation for a fix uncovers a platform quirk, sweep the messages and comments written in that same commit for claims the quirk falsifies before pushing.

evidence: 9540a64 guarded the three LOGFILE `mktemp` calls, which run after MSGFILE is written, with a message that never mentions the recorded handoff. The no-transport branch says 'preserved at: $MSGFILE' for the same outcome, and the new test covered only the pre-write GOALFILE arm. The agent added `RECORDED` interpolation and a selective-mktemp test, and confirmed the test fails without the fix.
guidance_note: When guarding several call sites with one helper, check which side of an irreversible write each site sits on, and test a site on each side.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: SKILL.md's stale invocation (`[message...]` with no `--` and no refusal note) dates from the original PR, and 9540a64 did not touch it. The same gap had been reported as an out-of-diff finding in the round 1 and round 2 summaries and went unaddressed until it landed inline. Fixed in 2316470.
guidance_note: When changing a CLI's argv grammar, grep every doc that shows the invocation (SKILL.md included) in the original PR, and act on 'findings outside the reviewed diff' in round summaries, not only on inline threads.

evidence: F6's fix guarded the four `mktemp` calls but left `printf > "$MSGFILE"` and `printf > "$GOALFILE"` unguarded under `set -e`. The agent reproduced exit 1 on an unwritable path, so the same class of 'exits 2' contract break remained. The agent swept the class into one `_refuse` enforcer, and reports tests that fail without it.
guidance_note: When fixing one instance of 'errexit leaks a non-contract status', enumerate every fallible statement in the arm (substitutions and redirections) in that same fix.

narrative: A small argv-refusal change ran to the five-round review cap, and round 5 went unreviewed. F1's fix broadened the exit-code line into an exhaustive contract that neither its 0-half (F5) nor the code (F6, unguarded mktemp under errexit) satisfied. F6's fix then spawned three more findings: a wrong directory in its own message (F8), a post-write path silent about the recorded handoff (F9), and the same unguarded-write class in two redirections (F11). Separately, the stale SKILL.md invocation was reported out-of-diff in rounds 1 and 2 and fixed only when it came back inline in round 3.
guidance_observations: The exit-code contract was written before it was verified against every implicit failure path, and each later round found another instance of the same class. A single errexit audit at F1 would have collapsed rounds 2 through 4.
Out-of-diff findings in review summaries were not acted on, which cost the SKILL.md fix at least one extra round.
The F2 pushback was contradicted by the agent's own F1 fix in the same commit, and the agent later reversed it. Cross-checking replies against the fixes in that push would have caught this.

evidence: The original block spelled out another skill's internals (the `SECRETS` table, `install.sh`, the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_<ACCOUNT>` keychain convention), which would drift. 5143942 reduced it to naming the setup skill's procedure. The 'pool may not exist' half is speculative, but the duplication was real.
guidance_note: When a procedure depends on another skill's mechanics, reference that skill's section by name from the first draft instead of summarising its internals.

evidence: The agent reported that the free-text grep for 'You've hit your limit' false-positived on this PR's own run, because the diff echoed the pattern. Anchoring was right, though the chosen anchor `##[error]rate-limited:` was itself free text, which F7 caught.
guidance_note: When detection reads a log that echoes the diff, anchor on a structured signal (check-run annotations) rather than any literal the doc itself must contain.

evidence: The block used `gh run view/rerun` inside the all-providers wait step, while `url` for other providers is not an Actions run. 5143942 scoped it to the `action` provider by name.
guidance_note: When adding provider-specific mechanics to a provider-agnostic step, gate them on the provider in the original draft.

evidence: The agent observed another session's rotation already in the table, so concurrent rotation is real, and declining a lock was reasonable. But the chosen fix (compare the named account against 'the one that just failed') needed a baseline the agent cannot read from a write-only secret, which F6 exposed.
guidance_note: Before writing a compare-then-act safeguard, confirm both sides of the comparison are observable; a write-only secret has no readable 'current' value.

evidence: F3's fix (5143942) wrote 'with one exception, for the `action` provider only, where the loop fixes the cause itself', which promises a blanket exception, while only the rate-limited sub-case is handled. ea24136 narrowed it and stated that the no-annotation fallback stops.
guidance_note: When writing an exception clause, name the exact condition the following mechanism handles and state the fallback for the rest of the same branch.

evidence: 5143942's step 1 ('If the named account is not the one that just failed, skip the rotation') needs to know the failed run's account, but the secret is write-only, as the agent conceded. The agent took the reviewer's 'drop the comparison' option: propagate, rerun, and rotate only on a second limit.
guidance_note: Check that every quantity a new safeguard compares is actually obtainable before committing the safeguard.

evidence: F2's fix anchored on the literal `##[error]rate-limited:` with `grep -F` over `--log-failed`. The SKILL.md now contains that literal, so a diff echo can match, which is the same failure mode F2 was fixing. 050716f moved detection to failure-level check-run annotations, which echoed text cannot mint.
guidance_note: When replacing a free-text anchor because it can be echoed, check whether the replacement literal will itself live in the echoed file; if so, use a structured API signal.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the stop condition with no bookkeeping ('Stop and surface only once every account in the pool has been tried') was in the original 0ef37ab text, and ea24136 only reworded the surrounding steps. Without a tried list the loop has no mechanical termination. 050716f added one.
guidance_note: Any 'repeat until all tried' loop in a procedure needs an explicit tried-set and termination test in the first draft.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: running the per-repo installer was in the original text ('run install.sh from this repo's root'). The agent confirmed the installer also converges `code-review.yml`, so a mid-loop tracked diff was possible and unaddressed. 050716f said what to do with it.
guidance_note: When a procedure invokes a generator for one side effect, check and document every file that generator writes.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 'say so with the reset time the log names' is in the original 0ef37ab text. After cycling several accounts, the last log's reset time is not necessarily the earliest. 050716f reports each tried account's reset time and the earliest.

F9's fix (050716f) introduced the literal `.github/workflows/code-review.yml`. Naming a path in prose so an agent knows which file to drop is a pointer, not a competing source of truth, and replacing it with 'the workflow file the installer reports writing' trades concreteness for nothing. Per the owner's review standard, a tie is rejected.

F8's fix attached 'Keep a list of the accounts you have landed on' to step 2 only, so step 1's account is never listed and the exhaustion check cannot be met. b32192e made step 1's account the first entry.
guidance_note: When adding bookkeeping for a termination test, trace the loop from its first iteration and confirm the test can actually become true.

evidence: F7's fix introduced `select(.conclusion=="failure")`. A cancelled or timed-out run then yields an empty `JOB_ID` and a malformed `check-runs//annotations` call, where the old grep simply found no match and fell through to stop-and-surface. b32192e changed it to `!="success"`.
guidance_note: When replacing a log grep with an API lookup, list every value of the field you filter on (cancelled, timed_out, startup_failure) and keep the 'no match, so stop' fallthrough for each.

evidence: The `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` literal was written by F1's fix (5143942), not by the flagged 050716f. Naming the secret the procedure acts on is a pointer that tells the agent what is out of quota, not a duplicated fact. The rewrite adds a parenthetical about which file 'owns that name' and buys nothing, so it is a tie the agent accepted.

F13 itself offered 'check for an empty JOB_ID before calling gh api'. The agent took only the broadened select, leaving `.jobs` empty (for example `startup_failure`) to produce the same malformed path. ae4e069 added the empty-id guard.
guidance_note: When a reviewer offers two guards for one failure, check whether the one you pick covers every case the other does before discarding it.

narrative: A 24-line skill-doc change hit the five-round review cap, and round 5 went unreviewed. Nearly every round after the first was spent on defects in the previous round's fixes. The detection anchor went from a free-text grep to another echoable literal (F7), then to an API lookup with an incomplete job filter (F13), then to a missing empty-id guard (F15). The concurrency safeguard compared against an unobservable value (F6), and the termination bookkeeping omitted step 1 (F12). The agent accepted every finding quickly, including two pedantic one-source-of-truth findings on prose pointers (F11, F14) that were ties.
guidance_observations: The agent shipped each fix within about a minute of planning it, without tracing the new procedure end to end, so every round found a defect in the last round's text.

Every finding after round 0 was accepted, including path-literal nits. Under the owner's tie-is-rejected rule, F11 and F14 should have been pushed back, which also stops the reviewer re-raising the same class.
The reviewer twice offered a second guard alongside its first suggestion (F13's empty-JOB_ID check), and taking only one guard cost the next round.
